Document identity, replicas, and contents

Source: R/doc.R
doc.Rd

  • doc_peer_id() returns the peer id of this replica as a string, and doc_set_peer_id() changes it. Two replicas must never edit under the same peer id.

  • doc_fork() returns an independent replica with the same history and a new peer id. With at, the replica holds the document as it was at that version.

  • doc_commit() commits pending edits as one change, optionally labeled with a message that is kept in the history and shown by doc_changes(). An origin is a label for this commit that is not stored or synchronized: it is passed to subscribers on this replica as event$origin, so they can tell where a change came from, and an undo manager can be told to ignore commits by origin. A timestamp is stored with the change in place of the current time, whether or not doc_record_timestamps() is on; Loro keeps timestamps non-decreasing, so one earlier than the latest existing timestamp is replaced by that latest one. Edits are also committed implicitly on export, import, and checkout.

  • doc_value() returns the whole document as a named list with one element per root container. It is an error if containers are nested more than 1000 levels deep.

  • doc_get() returns what is found by following a path into the document, one step per argument, as in doc_get(doc, "note", "items", 2): the name of a root container, then a string for each map key or tree node id (which leads to the node's metadata map) and a 1-based number for each list position. Containers are returned as handles, and NULL means nothing is there. Unlike doc_map() and its siblings, it never creates a container.

  • doc_jsonpath() returns a list of everything matching a JSONPath expression such as "$.note.items[*]". JSONPath is its own language, so list positions inside it are 0-based. Loro does not support every JSONPath feature: a query that has to descend into a tree container, or that uses the match() or search() functions, is an error.

Usage

doc_peer_id(doc)

doc_set_peer_id(doc, peer_id)

doc_fork(doc, at = NULL)

doc_commit(doc, message = NULL, origin = NULL, timestamp = NULL)

doc_value(doc)

doc_get(doc, ...)

doc_jsonpath(doc, path)

Arguments

doc

A loro_doc.

peer_id

A peer id: a whole number or a string of digits.

at

A version from doc_frontiers() to fork at, or NULL for the current version.

message

A string describing the change, or NULL.

origin

A string labeling the source of the commit, or NULL.

timestamp

The time to record for the commit, as a POSIXct or a number of seconds since 1970, or NULL.

...

The steps of a path: strings and whole numbers. These are dynamic dots, so a path held in a list can be spliced in with !!!.

path

A JSONPath expression, as a string.

Value

doc_set_peer_id() returns doc invisibly. doc_peer_id() returns a string, doc_fork() a new loro_doc, doc_commit() returns doc invisibly, and doc_value() a named list. doc_get() returns a value or container handle, and doc_jsonpath() a list of them.

Examples

doc = loro_doc(peer_id = 1)
text_insert(doc, 1, "Hello")
doc_peer_id(doc)
#> [1] "1"
doc_value(doc)
#> $text
#> [1] "Hello"
#> 

note = doc_map(doc, "note")
list_push(map_set_container(note, "items", "list"), "milk", "eggs")
doc_get(doc, "note", "items", 2)
#> [1] "eggs"
doc_jsonpath(doc, "$.note.items[*]")
#> [[1]]
#> [1] "milk"
#> 
#> [[2]]
#> [1] "eggs"
#>
